skill.name: module-scaffolder
skill.description: Scaffolds DevPrep AI feature modules with the required folder structure, TypeScript templates, path-alias guidance, and validation scripts.
skill.summary: Create and validate DevPrep AI feature modules with standard folder, TypeScript, and import conventions.
skill.author: ArieGoldkin

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from TypeScript import examples, Markdown code fences, and documented local helper scripts. Real issues remain in scripts that accept module names without consistent path validation, allowing path traversal for component writes or validation scans. No evidence of network exfiltration or prompt injection was found.

remediation.issue: Module names are not validated consistently across scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Add the same lowercase-with-hyphens validation used by create-module.sh to add-component.sh and validate-module.sh before building MODULE_PATH.

remediation.issue: Derived module paths can escape frontend/src/modules.
remediation.suggestion: Canonicalize MODULE_PATH with realpath or an equivalent check and reject any path that does not remain under MODULES_DIR before reading or writing files.

remediation.issue: Validation commands recursively scan a user-derived path.
remediation.suggestion: After path containment checks, limit validation to TypeScript files inside the target module and avoid printing unnecessary file contents or paths.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Module Path in Component Scaffolder
semantic_findings.description: scripts/add-component.sh accepts MODULE_NAME without the validation used by create-module.sh, builds MODULE_PATH from it, and writes a component file plus a barrel export. A crafted module name with ../ segments can target directories outside frontend/src/modules when matching folders exist.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script validates ComponentName but not MODULE_NAME, then uses MODULE_PATH for filesystem writes. The write target is constrained to component and index files, but path traversal can escape the intended module directory.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Module Path in Validation Script
semantic_findings.description: scripts/validate-module.sh accepts MODULE_NAME without validation and runs find, wc, and grep over the derived MODULE_PATH. A crafted ../ module name can make the validation routine inspect files outside the intended module tree.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The module path comes directly from user input and is used by recursive find and grep commands. The issue is read-oriented, so the severity is lower than the component write path.

content.value_statement: Creating a new feature module often requires repeated folders, exports, and TypeScript conventions. This skill generates the standard DevPrep AI module structure and checks it against project rules.
actual_capabilities: Creates DevPrep AI module folders for components, hooks, utils, and types.
Generates starter TypeScript and React files from bundled templates.
Adds a PascalCase component to an existing module and updates its barrel export.
Validates module structure, file length, interface naming, any usage, and relative imports.
Provides reference documentation for folder architecture, naming, path aliases, and quality checks.
limitations: Targets the DevPrep AI frontend/src/modules layout rather than arbitrary repositories.
Does not create API endpoints, database models, tests, or production feature logic.
Requires a Unix-like shell for the bundled helper scripts.
Generated files are starter templates and still need implementation.

use_cases.title: Start a New Feature Module
use_cases.description: Generate the baseline folder structure and starter files for a new DevPrep AI feature area.

use_cases.title: Standardize Module Conventions
use_cases.description: Use the references and validation script to keep module imports, interfaces, and file sizes consistent.

use_cases.title: Guide AI-Assisted Coding
use_cases.description: Give Claude, Codex, or Claude Code a concrete module pattern to follow before adding feature logic.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Module
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new feature area.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use module-scaffolder to create a notifications module. Generate the standard folders and starter TypeScript files, then summarize what was created.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Add UI structure to an existing module.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use module-scaffolder to add a NotificationCard component to the notifications module. Update the barrel export and list the next implementation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Module Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Use module-scaffolder to validate the analytics module. Report any structure, naming, file size, or import issues in clear language.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Multi-Module Rollout
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for a larger feature build.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use module-scaffolder references to plan modules for analytics, notifications, and user-profile. Identify shared code candidates and validation steps before scaffolding.

output_examples.output: The skill creates the analytics module folders, adds starter component and type files, creates barrel exports, and lists follow-up implementation steps.

output_examples.input: Add AnalyticsChart to the analytics module.
output_examples.output: The skill generates the new component file, updates the component export list, and reminds the user to define props and component logic.
The skill reports whether required folders and exports exist, whether files stay within size limits, and whether naming and import rules pass.

best_practices: Validate the module after scaffolding and before adding large feature logic.
Use path aliases for cross-folder imports and relative imports only within a module.
Rename or replace starter components once the real feature structure is clear.
anti_patterns: Using this skill for repositories that do not follow the DevPrep AI module layout.
Keeping generated placeholder content in production components.
Bypassing validation after adding components, hooks, or utilities.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a DevPrep AI feature module with components, hooks, utils, types, starter files, and barrel exports.

faq.question: Can it add more components later?
faq.answer: Yes. The add-component script generates a PascalCase component and updates the components export file.

faq.question: Does it write production-ready feature logic?
faq.answer: No. It creates starter structure and templates. Developers still need to implement behavior, data access, and tests.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What project layout does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects the DevPrep AI frontend module layout under frontend/src/modules.

faq.question: What should users check before running scripts?
faq.answer: Users should review the target module name and run the scripts only inside a trusted DevPrep AI repository.
